title: Schema-driven action proxy and robust stream gateway for SDK function calling
creator: Marco Valdez
description:
Scope: build an SDK-side "action proxy" and a resilient "stream gateway" that together provide cross-language helpers for: (1) validating function/action schemas supplied to the runtime, (2) canonicalizing invocation payloads across Python/TS/Go SDKs, and (3) managing robust streaming invocations with resumability and idempotent retry semantics.

Goal: reduce integration bugs and duplicated validation logic in apps by centralizing contract enforcement and stream orchestration inside the SDKs while keeping the runtime lightweight. Deliverables: SDK helper libraries (py/ts/go), contract test harness, docs/examples, and reference PRs integrating the helpers into the examples repo.

Design notes: 
- Schema model: adopt a JSON Schema-ish contract for parameter shapes plus a lightweight metadata layer for recommended coercions (e.g., parse_number, timestamp_iso). This avoids coupling to a single language type system.
- Validation: run best-effort client-side validation before sending; attach structured validation warnings to telemetry rather than failing calls by default. For strict mode, SDKs should throw on validation errors.
- Canonicalization: use canonical wire format (snake_case keys, explicit null vs absent) emitted by SDK adapters when the model signature uses non-language-native types.
- Streaming gateway: provide a small runtime in the SDK that handles: ordered chunk assembly, checkpointed resume tokens, and automatic backoff/reconnect logic when stream breaks mid-response. Resume tokens will be opaque strings issued by the runtime; SDK will persist them in-memory or via user callbacks for long-lived processes.
- Retry semantics: implement idempotency-key plumbing and an "at-least-once" default with optional exactly-once best-effort when an idempotency key is provided and the runtime supports it. Backoff: jittered exponential with capped attempts; make policy pluggable per-call.
- Cross-language ergonomics: expose idiomatic shims: async iterator for TS, generator + async for Python, and channel-friendly Go interface. Provide examples demonstrating how to integrate resume callbacks.
- Observability: emit structured events for validation failures, resume attempts, retry counts, and stream disconnect reasons to Redwood console (token-level metadata).

Acceptance criteria: 
- SDKs (py/ts/go) include the helper with tests covering validation, canonicalization, retry/backoff, and resume.
- Contract test harness validates the same sample schemas across all three SDKs and the runtime (end-to-end).
- Example app updated: examples/action-proxy-demo with both sync and streaming invocations for a mock "document-annotator" function.
- PRs: corresponding implementation PRs for each SDK + a docs PR describing migration/usage patterns.

Implementation notes and repo paths: 
- Python helper at sdk/python/redwood_sdk/actions/proxy.py and tests in tests/actions
- TS helper at sdk/js/src/actions/proxy.ts and tests in packages/sdk-js/test/actions
- Go helper at sdk/go/actions/proxy.go and tests in sdk/go/actions_test.go
- Contract harness at infra/contract-tests/action-proxy-harness

Risks & trade-offs: 
- Client-side validation can diverge from runtime validation; to mitigate we will run contract tests as part of CI and include an optional "strict" mode that mirrors the runtime behavior.
- Persisting resume tokens introduces surface area for sensitive values; treat tokens as non-sensitive but avoid logging them.

Next steps: prototype Python resume API and an end-to-end contract test with the dev runtime staging cluster.

2026-03-11 — Design review: PM + Runtime team suggested runtime provide opaque resume tokens and an explicit 'stream-resume' endpoint; adjust spec to rely on that. Action: add a 'resume_callback' hook in SDKs. (Aisha)

2026-03-12 — Spike results: Python prototype can resume a streaming response using a saved token; edge cases around partial chunk boundaries need unit tests. Added backlog item for chunk-framing edgecases. (Eng)

2026-03-13 — Security review request submitted; preliminary answer: resume tokens are okay as non-PII but must not be logged. Also requested that SDK avoid persisting tokens to disk by default. (Aisha)
